scope: Corollary 6.2 (Curve-class alternatives) of the manuscript “Deforming hypersymplectic four-manifolds to hyperkähler triples” (preprints/Deforming-hypersymplectic-four-manifolds-to-hyperkahler-triples-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 341 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 92c36602fb496808), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ˜︁ A, ˜︁ C be any smooth closed definite pair on X with [ ˜︁ A] = [A], [ ˜︁ C] = [C], and let J be either of its associated almost complex structures. For every nonconstant irreducible closed J-holomorphic curve whose class d ∈ Λ is nonzero, there is a real number c ̸= 0 with d+ = cF+. Exactly one of the following alternatives holds: (i) d · F ̸= 0, and sgn(d · F) = sgn(c) = sgn([B] · d); (ii) d = cF in Λ, with c ∈ Z \ {0}. If J admits a closed taming form, every nonconstant irreducible closed J-holomorphic curve has nonzero real class, so the nonzero-class hypothesis is automatic.
